series.title: JavaScript
stages: Integrating and verifying the experiment log

series.title: React
stages: Performance verification and an integrated editor

units.title: Values and State
units.goal: Extract 2 incomplete task titles. Record 2 pairs of reference equality and original value comparisons.

units.title: String input and number conversion
units.goal: Record the validation result and type of all four inputs. The saved count does not increase for whitespace or negative numbers.
units.exampleNote: Compare editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Equality Comparisons and Defaults
units.goal: Record 8 default-value outputs. Explain the comparison results for the same reference and different references.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Branches and Early Returns
units.goal: Record outputs for 3 normal cases and 2 error cases. Every returned object has an ok field.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Functions and Pure Calculations
units.goal: Neither NaN nor Infinity is displayed for the three inputs. Record 3 calculation results obtained without the DOM.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Scope and Closures
units.goal: Verify A=2 and B=1 in the independent implementation. Compare logs from the shared and independent implementations.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Array Aggregation and Empty Input
units.goal: Only the selected topic remains in the results, and the 5 original records are preserved. The sum for an empty array is 0, and the title list is an empty array.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Object Destructuring and Optional Access
units.goal: Display the information without exceptions whether contact details are present or absent. A missing name is not saved as a valid name.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Map and Set Indexes
units.goal: Record the tag counts before and after removing duplicates. Verify a lookup for a missing id and an update to an existing id separately.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Exceptions and Recovery Paths
units.goal: The busy state ends after both success and failure. Read valid input again after a failure.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Creating DOM Nodes and Inserting Text
units.goal: There are 3 li elements corresponding to 3 notes. The tag input does not create a strong element.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Event Propagation and Delegation
units.goal: Newly added items can also be deleted without individual listeners. A single click on a span leaves one processing log line.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Promises and Execution Order
units.goal: Record the actual order of the three types of logs. A reject is handled once in the final catch.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Asynchrony and Cancellation
units.goal: The second search term remains on screen even when responses finish in reverse order. Distinguish cancellation logs from ordinary failure logs.

units.title: Fetch Responses and HTTP Errors
units.goal: Check both the successful list and the 404 message. Record HTTP errors and JSON parsing errors separately.
units.exampleNote: Because preview network access is restricted, this example runs 200/404 fixtures using real Response objects. Test fetch and HTTP requests on a local server.

units.title: Parallel Work and Partial Failure
units.goal: Distinguish completion order from the order of the returned array. The partial-failure screen retains 2 successful items.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Debouncing and Timer Cleanup
units.goal: With the 300ms setting, there is 1 search call. There are 0 pending search calls after dispose.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Public Interfaces of ES Modules
units.goal: Call the calculations in state.js without the DOM. The initial list is displayed after the path is restored.
units.exampleNote: This example runs the public interface of a Blob ES module. Test actual separation into relative files and Network paths in an HTTP project.

units.title: Storage and Restore Failures
units.goal: The 3 note id values are the same before and after a refresh. The guidance differs for corrupted data and a valid empty list.
units.exampleNote: The practice-only key is removed after execution. SecurityError caused by the iframe storage policy is also displayed.

units.title: URL Filters and Back Navigation
units.goal: The address and selected filter match after a refresh. Restore the previous list after navigating back.
units.exampleNote: This example runs a URLSearchParams encoding round trip. Test the actual address bar and back navigation with popstate on a separate HTTP page.

units.title: FormData and Domain Validation
units.goal: A whitespace-only title is not added to the list. Record 2 pairs of collected entries for checked and unchecked states.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Exporting JSON with Blob
units.goal: The exported file contains 3 notes and a version value. Every generated object URL has a cleanup path.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: File Import and Structure Validation
units.goal: Restore exactly the number of items in a valid file. The existing id array is unchanged after rejection.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: State Transitions and Undo
units.goal: After 3 undo operations, id and completion values match the initial state. State is preserved for an unknown action.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: Storing Dates and Localized Display
units.goal: Record the two display values and the identical epoch value. Invalid dates are not saved.
units.exampleNote: Compare the editable inputs with actual browser execution results.

units.title: The box model and measured dimensions
units.goal: Record the actual widths of both cards. Distinguish the content, padding, border, and margin regions in the tools.
units.exampleNote: Change box-sizing to border-box and compare the measured widths of 244px and 200px. Document body/html selectors are scoped inside the Shadow DOM. @media responds to the outer preview viewport, while the width slider changes only the container. Network access, form navigation, and iframe execution are restricted.

units.title: Events and state snapshots
units.goal: Display 3 after functional updates starting from 0. Record the results of the plain-value update control separately.
units.exampleNote: This experiment uses the actual React API. It uses createElement instead of JSX.

units.title: Starting and target values
units.goal: Learning outcome: explain the roles of from and to. Input case: a card initially at x=40. Output: a transform table immediately after creation and after completion. Connect your explanation of initial application to the code.
units.exampleNote: This experiment explores starting and target values. You can manipulate it directly, and it cleans up the resources it uses.
